post.description: Answer the sign-in challenge of an enrolled account with an authenticator code or one single-use recovery code. Recovery codes are accepted from every role, including admin.

200.description: The challenged session is now fully authenticated.

401.description: The TOTP or recovery code was invalid or already consumed.

post.description: Consume one recovery code and rotate the signed-in account onto fresh MFA enrollment material, retiring the lost factor. Every other session is revoked, so the replacement is paired from this session alone. Available to every enrolled role, not administrators alone: the recovery code is the credential. An account that lost both its authenticator and its recovery codes needs the offline break-glass path instead (`sudo nexa mfa reset --user <name>`; see docs/runbooks/mfa-recovery.md).

200.description: The old factor was retired and replacement enrollment material was created.

401.description: The recovery code was invalid or already consumed.

429.description: Too many recovery attempts were made.

post.description: Turn off the second factor for the signed-in account, in any role including admin. Enrollment is optional, so disabling is a deliberate and audited choice — but it is gated like any sensitive action: the session must have completed an MFA challenge (step-up) and the request must carry the account password, so a stolen password alone can never strip MFA.

post.description: Change the signed-in account's password. Requires a fully authenticated session and the current password. On success the current session stays valid and the account's other sessions are revoked.

ClientError.description: The request was invalid, unauthenticated, unauthorized, rate-limited, or addressed a missing resource.

next.description: Where the client should go next. `mfa_enrollment` is an offer, not a gate: the session is already authenticated and the client may skip it. `mfa_challenge` is mandatory for an account with a confirmed factor — the session stays unauthenticated until the challenge is answered. `authenticated` means no further step is needed.

mfaEnabled.description: Whether the current session's account has a confirmed second factor.

mfaChallengeRequired.description: Whether the enrolled account must answer its second-factor challenge before the session is authenticated. This is never skippable.

mfaEnrollmentRecommended.description: Whether the authenticated account has no second factor and could add one. Enrollment is optional for every role, including admin, so this is a recommendation the client may surface but must never block on.

bootstrapTokenRequired.description: Whether a remote bootstrap request must include the server-issued bootstrap token.

Error.description: Shared error envelope returned by every non-2xx JSON response.

offset.description: Present on upload offset conflicts; the next byte offset the server expects.

siteIds.description: Sites granted to a developer; empty for unscoped roles.

deploymentMode.description: Who owns the document root: the panel (standard) or a release tree the deployer publishes into (deployer). Always present on a site read.

SitePlan.description: A signed node configuration plan. This endpoint is readable with sites.read, so basic-auth credential material is withheld from the response: the passwordHash field is empty and the password file's body, before-state, and digest read "[redacted]". Only the response is redacted — the stored plan keeps the real credential, which the node needs to re-render the file byte-identically when the plan is applied.

retired.description: Managed paths this site must not have once the plan is applied — the conditional artifacts (rate-limit zone, htpasswd file, logrotate stanza) whose setting is currently off. The node re-derives this list from the plan's settings and refuses any path it would not itself have produced, so a plan can only ever delete files the operator owns for this site.

retiredBefore.description: Pre-apply snapshots of the retired paths, so a rollback can restore whatever the removal took away.

SiteSettings.description: Per-site Nginx/PHP-FPM tuning. Every field is optional; an absent field falls back to a hardened default, so an empty object ({}) re-renders the baseline configuration identically.

phpVersion.description: Write-only, and only meaningful on the settings update: change the site's PHP runtime. The version must be installed and enabled on the node. The next apply moves the site's FPM pool to the new version and retires the outgoing one. Absent (or equal to the current version) leaves the runtime untouched; the field is never emitted on reads — the site's own phpVersion property reports the runtime.

hsts.description: Emit an HTTP Strict-Transport-Security response header.

hstsMaxAge.description: HSTS max-age in seconds; only used when hsts is enabled. An explicit 0 (or absent) falls back to 15552000 (180 days).

http2.description: Enable HTTP/2. Absent defaults to on.

http3.description: Enable HTTP/3 (QUIC). Absent or false defaults to off.

httpsRedirect.description: Redirect plain HTTP to HTTPS with a 301 on the port-80 server block. Absent defaults to true, which is the historical behaviour; an explicit false makes port 80 serve the site directly instead. The setting only has an effect once the site has a TLS certificate, and the ACME challenge location stays reachable over plain HTTP either way, so certificate issuance and renewal are unaffected. Note that an absent value and an explicit true render identically; OpenAPI cannot express that "absent means on" on a plain boolean, so it is documented here in prose (the same convention used for http2).

subdirectory.description: Document root to serve, relative to the site's public/ directory (for example `dist` or `app/public`). Absent or empty serves public/ itself. It is public-relative rather than site-root-relative on purpose: the site's logs/, private/, tmp/, and backups/ directories are siblings of public/, so a root-relative value could publish them. Traversal (`..`), absolute paths, and non-canonical values are rejected, and the directory is created on the node when the setting is applied.

charset.description: Character set advertised by Nginx for this site. Absent or empty emits no `charset` directive at all, leaving the character set entirely to the application's own Content-Type header — that is the default and it is byte-identical to the configuration Nexa generated before this setting existed. An explicit `off` emits `charset off;`, which differs from absent only in that it also overrides a charset inherited from the server-wide http{} configuration. Values are lowercased server-side and must be one of the enumerated tokens; arbitrary charset names are rejected so the token can never escape the directive.

gzip.description: Enable gzip response compression. Absent defaults to on.

gzipLevel.description: gzip compression level. 0 or absent falls back to 5.

staticCacheDays.description: Number of days to cache static assets via an expires header. Absent defaults to 30. An explicit 0 emits no expires header, which differs from absent; OpenAPI cannot express that distinction on a plain integer, so it is documented here in prose.

clientMaxBodyMb.description: Nginx client_max_body_size in megabytes (note the lowercase 'b' in the key). Absent defaults to 64.

pmMode.description: PHP-FPM process manager mode. Absent defaults to ondemand.

pmMaxChildren.description: PHP-FPM pm.max_children. 0 or absent falls back to 3.

pmMaxRequests.description: PHP-FPM pm.max_requests. Absent defaults to 500. An explicit 0 means unlimited, which differs from absent; OpenAPI cannot express that distinction on a plain integer, so it is documented here in prose.

accessLog.description: Write the Nginx access log for this site. Absent defaults to on.

errorLog.description: Write the Nginx error log for this site. Absent defaults to on.

indexFiles.description: Ordered list of application files Nginx tries when a directory is requested (the `index` directive). Absent or empty renders the baseline `index.php index.html`. Entries must be plain filenames — no directory separators, no traversal, no leading dot — and are emitted in exactly the order given, which is the order Nginx tries them. Duplicates are rejected. The first entry ending in `.php` also becomes the front controller that `location /` falls back to; when no entry ends in `.php` the fallback stays `index.php`.

workingDirectory.description: PHP-FPM `chdir` for this site's worker processes, relative to the SITE ROOT (for example `public` or `app`). Absent or empty chdirs to the site root itself. This is a different axis from `subdirectory`, which is relative to public/ and selects the document root Nginx publishes: this setting publishes nothing, it only sets a worker's initial working directory, so it may legitimately name a directory outside public/. Traversal (`..`), absolute paths, and non-canonical values are rejected, and the directory is created on the node when the setting is applied. Depth is capped at 8 segments.

realm.description: HTTP basic-auth realm. Absent or empty falls back to "Restricted".

password.description: Plaintext password, hashed server-side. An empty value on save keeps the current password. Always empty on read.

DatabaseEngine.description: Engine family a server or resource belongs to.

DatabaseServer.description: One database server on the node — the discovered MySQL-family engine or a PostgreSQL instance.

CreateDatabaseServer.description: Provision a new server instance on an engine that supports it (PostgreSQL today; the MySQL-family engine is discovered, not provisioned).

host.description: Client host scope; MySQL-family servers only.

password.description: Chosen or generated in the client and applied to the engine as-is; the panel stores only its ciphertext and digest.

siteId.description: Optional site this database belongs to; site teardown blocks on the relation.

package.description: The apt package the suffix resolves to for this branch, e.g. php8.3-redis

module.description: The extension (module) that registers the directive; "core" for the engine itself

value.description: The effective value under the FPM SAPI (including any nexa-managed override)

managed.description: Whether nexa's managed drop-in (or, per-site, the .user.ini) currently overrides this directive

SavePhpSettings.description: Directives to set to a value, and directives to reset to their default

version.description: PHP branch to save (branch-wide settings only; omitted for per-site saves)

expectedEtag.description: Entity tag from the last read; an empty or missing value writes unconditionally.

cronExpression.description: Exactly five numeric cron fields; names such as @daily or MON are rejected.

SshAccess.description: Interactive SSH access for one site, delivered through that site's Unix Owner. The key bodies are never returned; the fingerprint is the identity a human compares.

shell.description: The login shell the account currently has

authorizedKeysPath.description: The root-owned authorized-keys file the Match block names; it deliberately lives outside the site's home

algorithm.description: Key type as sshd names it, e.g. ssh-ed25519

GeneratedSshKey.description: The one and only response carrying a private key. It is generated for the caller, never stored, and cannot be retrieved again.

DeployKey.description: The site's Git deploy key. The pair is minted on the node and only the public half ever reaches the control plane, so `present` rather than a non-empty publicKey is what says a key exists.

publicKey.description: The public half, ready to register as a repository deploy key

repository.description: The SSH remote this site deploys from, e.g. git@github.com:owner/name.git

DeploymentModeChange.description: A job is present whenever the site was live enough to need re-applying; without one the mode is stored and the site's next plan picks it up.

SharedEnv.description: The deployer layout's shared environment file. Its content is a secret in both directions - it is never logged, never audited, and never carried in a job payload.

DeployTool.description: One prerequisite as the preparation run found - or left - it. A tool that could not be installed is a result, not a failed job.

FirewallSshCheck.description: The read-only port-22 verdict. `checked` false means the panel could not ask, which is a fact about the panel and never means the port is closed.

remediation.description: The exact command an operator can run; the preparation never runs it, because opening a port belongs behind firewall.write

NodePreparation.description: The preparation job's result. `ready` covers the tooling only - the firewall is a warning surface, not something this job clears.

siteIds.description: Site scope used to enforce developer grants; omitted for unscoped jobs.

attempt.description: Number of worker leases claimed for this job.

request.description: Kind-specific JSON payload; it may be an object, array, scalar, or null. Credential-shaped fields (password, secret, token, key, passphrase, and similar) are replaced with the string "[redacted]" on the response path.

result.description: Kind-specific JSON result; it may be an object, array, scalar, or null. Redacted the same way as request.

version.description: Target release version; empty installs the latest.

PasswordPolicy.description: The set-time password policy the server enforces, published so sign-up and password-change forms can render exactly the same requirements. The denylist itself is never exposed, only the fact that one is applied.

requiredClasses.description: How many of lowercase, uppercase, digit and symbol a password must mix.

classExemptLength.description: Length at or above which a passphrase is exempt from the character-class rule.

denylistApplied.description: Whether common and predictable passwords are rejected.

rejectsUsername.description: Whether a password containing the account's username is rejected.

SiteLogRotation.description: Optional logrotate stanza for the site's own logs (logs/access.log, logs/error.log, logs/php-error.log). Absent or disabled emits no file at all, which is the historical behaviour: Nexa does not rotate site logs unless this is turned on.

enabled.description: Write /etc/logrotate.d/nexa-<slug>. Disabling it stops the panel from managing the file on the next apply.

keepFiles.description: Number of rotated copies to keep before the oldest is discarded (logrotate `rotate N`). 0 or absent falls back to 14.

frequency.description: Rotation interval. Absent or empty falls back to daily. `hourly` is only honoured if the node invokes logrotate hourly; the Debian/Ubuntu default logrotate.timer fires once a day, in which case an hourly stanza rotates at most once per day.

repository.description: The SSH remote; empty keeps whatever the panel already stored

rotate.description: Replace the pair itself, invalidating the key the repository already trusts

content.description: The whole file; at most 65536 bytes
